newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bank stocks near record highs.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bank stocks near record highs.

text.p: Most Portuguese bank shares are close to record highs and could rise further because of expectations of strong results this year and buy recommendations by investment houses, analysts said on Thursday.
They said the forthcoming privatisation of a 30 percent stake of state utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal on June 16 would help bank results.
Many people have applied for EDP shares at retail bank branches, earning the banks commissions. The EDP privatisation was many times oversubscribed, market sources said.

"The rise of bank shares is linked to the good fundamentals of the sector and we expect that banks involved in the EDP sale will make a lot of money out of it," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified,

Diego Hernando of Lisbon broker Midas said: "Bank shares do not seem expensive in relation to their historic performance and there are good prospects for results. It is natural that the bank shares will continue to do well."

Banco Comercial Portugues hit an all-time high of 3,280 escudos on Thursday. Banco Portugues de Investimento was trading just short of its record high of 2,888 escudos reached on May 13. Banco Espirito Santo (BES) hit a record high of 3,675 escudos on Thursday.

Two exceptions were Banco Pinto e Sotto Mayor, standing at 1,777 escudos in late trade, compared with its record high of 1,398 escudos reached on February 13, and Banco Totta e Acores, trading at 2,480, compared with its all-time high of 3,220 touched on January 16.
Since December 1996, BCP and BPI shares have risen by about 50 percent and BES by about 35 percent.

BPSM shares grew by around 10 percent and BTA fell by about 15 percent over the same period. Analysts said the restructuring of BPSM and a decision by BTA to pursue a less generous dividend policy had penalised the stocks.
Banking stocks have benefited from buy recommendations by investment house Salomon. Salomon recommended BCP, BPI and BTA as a "strong buy" and BES as a "buy." It recommended BPSM as a "hold."
Salomon gave target prices in the next 10 months of 3,700 escudos for BCP, 3,800 for BPI, 3,400 for BTA, 3,750 for BES and 1,350 for BPSM.
Analysts said both BCP and BPI were benefiting from the rapid restructuring of the groups after their respective acquisitions of Banco Portugues do Atlantico and Banco de Fomento e Exterior.

"The banking sector will be helped by the improvement of the economy, there is a reduction of costs due to the restructuring of some banks and so we are seeing a positive impact for the results and share prices in 1997," said Miguel Viana, analyst with CFI-Sociedade Corretora of the Champalimaud group.
An analyst with an investment bank said: "The strong overall economic growth will allow the banks to hand out more credit, and bad loans will drop."
